questions.question:
D4 — Which review mode for the saved-views plan? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-mode>
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count fixture on main, PLAN.md with approach B (versioned filter-spec views) approved.
ELI10: The mode sets my posture for the rest of the review. Expansion means I pitch the ambitious version and you opt in item by item. Selective expansion means I make the current scope bulletproof and separately show you expansion candidates to cherry-pick with no sales pitch. Hold scope means rigor only, no new ideas. Reduction means I cut to the smallest thing that removes the pain. Whatever you pick, no scope changes without your explicit yes.
Stakes if we pick wrong: too expansive and a two-week pilot feature grows sharing and defaults before anyone has used it; too narrow and obvious adjacent wins (a default view, a dirty-state prompt) never get considered.
Recommendation: B (Selective Expansion) because this iterates on an existing task list, and the landscape shows adjacent features (shared views, default view) that deserve a look but should not be assumed.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
A) Scope Expansion
  ✅ Surfaces the full cathedral: shared views, project defaults, view-driven digests, in one pass
  ✅ Best when the feature is greenfield and the team wants the 10x version now
  ❌ Pushes hard toward more scope before the pilot has proven anyone reuses a view
B) Selective Expansion (recommended)
  ✅ Holds approach B as the baseline and reviews it with full rigor first
  ✅ Presents each expansion candidate individually with neutral effort and risk so you cherry-pick
  ❌ More decision prompts than Hold Scope; roughly 5-6 extra questions
C) Hold Scope
  ✅ Fastest path: architecture, security, edge cases, observability, deployment only
  ✅ Zero risk of scope creep before the pilot
  ❌ Adjacent 30-minute wins are never raised, even ones the landscape says drive adoption
D) Scope Reduction
  ✅ Finds the smallest shippable slice, useful if the pilot is purely a signal test
  ✅ Separates must-ship-together from nice-to-have follow-up PRs
  ❌ Conflicts with the approach B you just approved, which deliberately closes silent failure modes
Net: how many adjacent ideas you want to see before the rigorous pass, versus decision fatigue.

options.label: B: Selective Expansion (Recommended)
options.description: Rigorous review of approach B, then individual cherry-pick questions for expansions.

options.label: A: Scope Expansion
options.description: Dream big; each ambitious proposal presented for opt-in.

options.label: C: Hold Scope
options.description: Maximum rigor on current scope, no expansions surfaced.

options.label: D: Scope Reduction
options.description: Strip to the minimum that removes the pain, then review that.
